content_voiceover: This slide is a Chinese-language excerpt on preventive treatment strategy for hemophilia B, and it highlights four key differences between hemophilia A and B that make excellent board material. First, prevalence differs substantially. Hemophilia A affects about one in five thousand males, while hemophilia B affects only about one in thirty thousand, making it roughly six times rarer. Second, the common genetic defects differ. In hemophilia A, large defects like the intron twenty-two inversion account for about forty-five percent of cases, with missense mutations at about fifteen percent. In hemophilia B, it's nearly reversed, large defects are under ten percent, while missense mutations dominate at fifty-eight percent. Third, severe disease makes up about fifty percent of hemophilia A cases but only about thirty percent of hemophilia B cases. And fourth, inhibitor rates differ dramatically, twenty to thirty percent in hemophilia A versus only three to five percent in hemophilia B.
keypoints: Hemophilia B is about six times rarer than hemophilia A
Intron 22 inversion dominates hemophilia A mutations, missense mutations dominate hemophilia B
Severe disease is more common in hemophilia A than hemophilia B
Inhibitor rates are far higher in hemophilia A than hemophilia B
keypoint_voiceover: The four differences to memorize are prevalence, hemophilia B is much rarer, mutation type, hemophilia A is dominated by large gene defects while hemophilia B is dominated by missense mutations, severity, hemophilia A has more severe cases, and inhibitor rate, which is much higher in hemophilia A.
